newsitem.title: USA: N.H. Gov proposes tax for time-shares, condos.
newsitem.headline: N.H. Gov proposes tax for time-shares, condos.

text.p: New Hampshire Gov. Jeanne Shaheen on Tuesday defended her plan to double the state's tourism promotion by making time-share condominium maintenance agreements subject to the meals and rooms tax.

Shaheen said that by "closing a loophole" in the tax and ending exemptions for time-share rentals, the state will be able to raise enough funds to increase its tourism advertising budget from $1.7 million to $3.3 million annually by fiscal year 1999.

"Last year, visitors pumped almost $2.7 billion into the state's economy," Shaheen said, adding, "By doubling the state's advertising budget, I hope to ensure that tourism will continue to be a dynamic and expanding sector of our economy into the next century."

The state meals and rooms tax is currently set at eight percent. The Department of Revenue Administration said the governor's proposal will increase state general fund revenue by $1.664 million in fiscal 1998 and by $1.728 million by fiscal 1999.

The funds will be used to increase international tourism promotion and out-of-state advertising. Some funds will be used by the New Hampshire Film Bureau to help attract feature film producers to the state.
The Democrat governor's proposal won immediate support from the state's hospitality industry.
But Republicans blasted the proposal as a "new tax" and said it would be used for other purposes besides tourism.

"This is not a tax on meals and this is not a tax on rooms. The monthly condominium fee...pays for snow removal, lawn mowing, electricity and other similiar operating expenditures," said GOP chairman Steve Duprey.
